subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 2-year-old boy is evaluated for recurrent pneumonia, chronic diarrhea, and failure to thrive. Laboratory studies show markedly decreased serum IgG, IgA, and IgE with an elevated serum IgM; B-cell and T-cell numbers are normal. Flow cytometry shows that his B cells express surface IgM and IgD but not IgG, IgA, or IgE. Genetic testing identifies a mutation in CD40 ligand (CD40L).
question: Which of the following processes is most directly impaired in this patient?

options.text: V(D)J recombination of immunoglobulin heavy-chain and light-chain variable regions
Somatic hypermutation of variable-region genes in germinal centers
Assembly and signaling of the pre-B-cell receptor
Proteolytic cleavage of immunoglobulin into Fab and Fc fragments
Class switch recombination of heavy-chain constant-region genes

explanation_correct: Interaction of CD40L on helper T cells with CD40 on B cells is required for class switch recombination, which joins a new heavy-chain constant region to the existing variable region and changes the isotype from IgM and IgD to IgG, IgA, or IgE. Loss of this signal leaves normal numbers of B cells that produce only IgM, the pattern of X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome.

explanation_incorrect.A: Defective V(D)J recombination prevents assembly of any functional antigen receptor, producing absent B cells and panhypogammaglobulinemia (as in Bruton agammaglobulinemia) rather than normal B cells with isolated IgM production.
explanation_incorrect.B: Somatic hypermutation introduces point mutations that increase antibody affinity for antigen; impaired affinity maturation would not change the isotype distribution or raise IgM.
explanation_incorrect.C: Failure of pre-B-cell receptor assembly blocks B-cell development before surface immunoglobulin expression, so B cells would be absent rather than IgM-positive.
explanation_incorrect.D: Cleavage of immunoglobulin into Fab and Fc fragments is an in vitro effect of papain digestion, not a physiologic step that determines the antibody class.

educationalObjective: X-linked hyper-IgM syndrome results from defective CD40L-CD40 interaction and impaired class switch recombination, leaving elevated IgM with low IgG, IgA, and IgE.
